title: Pair donors to avoid parity erasure on the source-assisted v4 word: conditional κ = 6.647872e-4
body:
## Result

Conditional κ = 103873/156250000 = **0.0006647872**. This is about 0.438% above PR186 (0.000661885549259598) and 0.325% above PR191 (0.0006626307).

The complex saving is b = 219037/312500000 = 0.0007009184. PR184's effective bit saving, about 0.00066522948, is now smaller, so the bit supplier binds.

## What changed

This PR adds one commit to PR191. PR191 runs PR184's source-parity local word and source-assisted frame flow on PR168 v4's query modules and physical layer.

PR184 pairs each live gauge (recipient) with an earlier donor role by a plain maximum bipartite matching. Its flow then erases some donors with original-source X controls at cube parity frames. Here `source_aligned_local_v4.py --avoid-parity-erasure` takes a minimum-weight full matching of the recipients instead. A pair costs 2 if the parity purification could erase it, and 1 otherwise.

With the frozen pairs in `data/physical-pairs.json`, the flow erases no donor and reuses no kernel. It finds 8,116 dependent outgoing values instead of 10,364, so it needs 1,412 fewer dirty births.

| Quantity | PR184 (fd25adb7 modules) | PR191 (v4 modules) | This PR (v4 modules, new pairs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Physical auxiliaries R | 11,056 | 10,824 | 9,412 |
| Persistent roles W | 13,696 | 13,464 | 12,052 |
| Source-controlled erasures | 1,410 | 1,412 | 0 |
| Zero-fresh kernel reuses | 706 | 707 | 0 |
| Complex saving | 6.570752e-4 | 6.630702e-4 | 7.009184e-4 |
| κ | 6.566436e-4 | 6.626307e-4 | 6.647872e-4 |

Any legal pairing is allowed. `paired_cube_physical.physical()` checks the frozen pairs. PR184's exact lift and contract checks pass unchanged on the new flow: all fresh columns equal the identity over the integers, source controls sit at paid parity frames, centers finish in phase 1, target cap reads occur in phase 2, and target chains nest.

The complex side now has about 5% of slack over the bit side. A stronger bit supplier would raise κ further, up to the complex saving.

## Verify

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/source-assisted/requirements-round13.txt
python3 -B research/source-assisted-v4/verify.py
```

It takes about one minute. It regenerates the v4 cache and the new local word with the frozen pairs, runs PR184's flow, exact lift and assembly unchanged, runs this package's copy of PR184's contract checker, and compares the result with `certificate.json`. The workflow `.github/workflows/source-assisted-v4.yml` runs it in CI.

## Branch

The branch stacks on PR191, which stacks on PR185's head `32daefe471e1e41926971747bb901e2839938b43` with PR184's commit merged. A separate commit in PR191 only updates the shared-file hashes that the merge made stale.

## Scope

PR184's validation scope applies. The exact lift and the contract checks establish the local maps and the flow ledger. There is no globally renumbered scalar transcript of the new complex word and no full Clifford/router replay. The bit supplier and its scope are PR184's. The analytic, recursion, precision, weighted frame, fixed-tape routing, restored-row and all-size interfaces stay as assumptions. The PR192 frame ceiling covers only PR168's fixed word and pairs, so it does not apply to this word.
